Red Dragon (CV 104)

An immense red-scaled dragon with a horned head, broad wings and a furnace-bright throat. Intelligent and deeply possessive, it treats territory, tribute and reputation as parts of the same hoard.

Attributes: Brawn +2; Fortitude +2; Agility +1; Guile +2; Knowledge +2; Reason +2

HP: 56 · Speed: 7; fly 10 · Size: 3 (3x3 squares) · Armor DR: 3*

Evasion: None · Threat: 2 Banes · Stability: 2

Weaknesses: None\ Resistances: Physical (3), Fire (3)\ Immunities: None

Actions

Damage and effects are Weak / Standard / Strong player defense. Each slash separates one complete outcome. All attacks use the printed Threat unless stated otherwise.

Details

Claw sweep

A great limb scythes across the ground, forcing everyone nearby to move.

Target: Up to two creatures within 2 squares. Player defense: Agility. Damage type: physical.

Weak defense: Push each 4. Standard defense: Push each 2.

Furnace breath

Its chest swells and light leaks between its teeth; there is one terrible instant to scatter.

Target: All creatures in a cone of 3 rows, 1/3/5 squares wide. Player defense: Agility. Damage type: fire.

Weak defense: Burning 2. Standard defense: Burning 1.

Limit: Cannot use this attack on consecutive turns, regardless of result.

Crushing bite

The dragon’s jaws close with the weight of a falling portcullis.

Target: One creature within 2 squares. Player defense: Fortitude. Damage type: physical.

Weak defense: Bleeding 2. Standard defense: Bleeding 1.

Tail Retort

The dragon twists with the blow and its heavy tail sweeps across the attacker's footing.

After an adjacent attacker's attack resolves and deals HP damage to this creature, push that attacker 2 squares directly away. This creature must survive and remain capable. Apply Stability, terrain costs and normal collision damage; no separate attack damage. Cannot trigger from a free attack or another retaliatory effect.

General details

Basic Melee: One adjacent creature; physical damage; Agility defense. Uses the printed Threat. No specialty riders.

Defend: Player attacks suffer 1 additional Bane until the start of its next turn. Combines with Evasion through normal Boon/Bane rules. Repeated Defend does not stack.

Opportunity Attack: Basic Melee against the provoking creature. Spends its Reaction before the provoking action resolves. That action continues if the creature remains capable.

Heavy Frame — Passive: Stability 2; an explicit creature trait, not a bonus from size.

Healing: Living: ordinary HP healing applies.

Senses: Ordinary sight and hearing.

Signs: Tribute wagons arrive on a schedule; the countryside knows which bells not to ring.

Purpose: Keep a domain profitable, obedient and impressed.

Tactics and retreat: Open with breath against a cluster, then sweep defenders away from cover; demand terms if the hoard is threatened.

Counterplay and conversation: Spread out, contest the hoard or escape route, and bring a bargain with something it cannot simply take.

Habitat: Mountain fortress; volcanic valley · Communication: Common and Draconic

Loot: A single adventure hoard: propose 400 coins plus one reviewed special item, not an item on every scale.

Summoning: Ineligible.

Design notes — not needed during play

The incoming attack names the defense attribute; use the six values above. Same targeting, costs and limits apply in either perspective. No opposed second roll.

CV worksheet

Difficulty rationale: No innate attack modifier; armor, cover and chosen actions provide its defenses. Its dangerous attack imposes defense Banes.

Reference damage: 5/7/10

Reference type: physical

Expected targets: 2

Utility factor: 1.75

Action review (#1279): U 1.6 → 1.75: Maneuver allowance +0, Reaction allowance +0.15. These are provisional judgments for the changed capabilities, counting the largest increment in each category rather than adding every alternative. Reactions compete for one budget; no measured balance claim.

Regeneration per turn: 0

Reference I=2.162, O=15.075. CV uses the seed worksheet; action choices, Stability and control are not simulated. Recalibration remains required.
